title: copilot-proxy-rs: /v1/systemone answers the other questions when the model declines one
prompt:
POST /v1/systemone (added in #62, src/http/systemone.rs and src/translate/systemone.rs) returns HTTP 422 `model declined to answer question(s): <names>` for the WHOLE request when the upstream model declines even one question (SystemOneError::Refused). The upstream reply still has answers for the other questions, but the client gets none. Measured with gpt-6-luna-decisions (upstream /v1/decisions) on 70 real software-factory decision calls (2-20 questions each): 3 calls failed this way, losing 18 answers to 1 refused question per call (example: `model declined to answer question(s): cr4_real`, in a call with 16 finding questions). The factory then treats every question in the call as unanswered and takes its fail-safe path for all of them. microsoft-decision-1 (upstream /v1/systemone) had no refusals in the same run.

Goal: one declined question no longer fails the others.
1. Research first: the exact per-question refusal shape of upstream /v1/decisions and /v1/systemone (the #62 research found per-question refusals; recorded fixtures exist in tests/fixtures/systemone_mixed.json and the refusal_mixed case). Check whether the TypeSafe systemOne API (@typesafe-ai/sdk, the shape /v1/systemone copies) defines a refusal answer; if it does, use that shape. Record findings in the PR body.
2. Return 200 with every answered question in `answers`, as today. For each declined question, return an entry the client can tell apart from an answer and that a Jev-shaped client ignores safely: preferably `answers.<name> = {"type": "refusal", "refusal": "<upstream text or 'declined'>"}` with no noul/choice field (or the TypeSafe shape if it defines one). Return the error only when the model declined every question: keep 422 and the current message for that case. Keep 400/413/502 behavior unchanged. Same for both decision models.
3. Logging: keep the existing warn line for full rejections; for partial refusals log one info/warn line with the count of declined questions and their names only (no prompts, state, or bodies).
4. README: document the refusal entry and when 422 still happens.
5. Tests: contract tests with recorded-shape fixtures (synthetic values) for both models: one of several declined (200, others answered, refusal entry), all declined (422), none declined (unchanged). cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked pass with no Cargo.lock change.
6. Proof on port 18080 (COPILOT_PROXY_RS_PORT=18080, COPILOT_PROXY_RS_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/copilot-proxy-rs so the existing config.toml and token are read in place; never copy a token or config file, the shell refuses it). Live refusals are not guaranteed: try to trigger one with gpt-6-luna-decisions (e.g. a batch of normal questions plus one the model is likely to decline, such as a question with no basis in the state); if you cannot trigger one live in 10 attempts, say so and rely on the contract tests. Also show one normal 40-question batch per model still returns 200 with 40 answers. Put results under "Proof" in the PR body.
- Never touch, stop or bind the live proxy on 8080. Keep log_failed_request_bodies behavior unchanged. Do not log tokens, prompts or bodies.
- Keep research notes and raw captures out of the PR (no reports/ files committed).
- This is a repeatable factory test: other open PRs for related work are earlier runs. Ignore them and build a new PR.
